<reason>B offered the stronger portfolio comparison: unavoidable crew-support costs and large, indivisible architectures explain why the proposed transfer could appropriately be substantial. A established genuine complementary and option value, and correctly challenged B's exclusion of future rebuilding costs, but did not show those benefits plausibly outweigh the forgone robotic science. B's flagship-scale explanation answered “why most?” sufficiently to survive A's demand for more specific mission comparisons, though not decisively enough for a large margin.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B distinguished Hubble's near-Earth servicing value from the case for expensive deep-space crewed architectures: a useful complement does not establish its appropriate budget share. A's subsequent inability to identify a deep-space science-per-dollar winner strengthened that response, without eliminating A's legitimate rebuilding-cost objection.</best_rebuttal>
